transcript.text: Just got a new Siemens dishwasher and there's always a bit of water left in the bottom under the filter after it finishes. Is it draining properly?

A small amount of clean water remaining under the filter after a cycle is actually normal; it keeps the internal seals lubricated and prevents odours. However, if there is a large puddle, dirty water, or if dishes are coming out wet/dirty, it suggests a drainage issue like a blocked filter or a kinked hose. To check this safely, please switch off and unplug the dishwasher first. Then remove the lower rack, twist and lift out the main filter in the bottom of the tub. Is there just a small amount of clean water (a cup or so) around the sump area, or is it significantly more? Also, was the filter itself clogged with food or debris?
[Helpful to see: image "Where the filter is" — The filter sits in the base of the dishwasher, usually under the bottom spray arm. Twist it out anticlockwise and rinse it under a tap. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]
Thanks! I've had a look: it's just about a cupful of clean water covering the bottom of the sump under the filter, and none in the main tub. The filter itself is clean, no food or debris on it.

That suggests it is normal. A small amount of clean water (about a cup) sitting under the filter after the cycle finishes is designed to keep the internal seals lubricated and prevent odours. There is no large puddle, and the filter itself is clear, your dishwasher is draining correctly and there is no fault to fix.
